source: International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome 2023 (Teede et al., Hum Reprod 2023;38(9):1655-1679)
text: PCOS should be diagnosed using the revised 2003 Rotterdam Criteria, requiring 2 of 3 features in adults: 1) ovulatory dysfunction (irregular or absent cycles), 2) clinical and/or biochemical hyperandrogenism, 3) polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound or elevated Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH), with exclusion of other etiologies (thyroid disease, hyperprolactinemia, non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia).

source: International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS 2023 (Teede et al., Hum Reprod 2023)
text: A comprehensive medical history and physical examination should be conducted for clinical signs of hyperandrogenism, specifically terminal hair hirsutism, severe acne, and female pattern hair loss. Severe hirsutism in adults is strongly predictive of biochemical hyperandrogenism and PCOS. Rapid onset or progressive worsening of virilizing androgen features requires prompt medical investigation to exclude androgen-secreting tumors or non-PCOS etiologies.

source: Ferriman D, Gallwey JD. Clinical assessment of body hair growth in women. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 1961;21:1440-1447
text: The modified Ferriman-Gallwey (mFG) visual scoring method grades terminal hair growth across 9 body sites from 0 (no terminal hair) to 4 (extensive growth). Cut-offs vary by ethnicity, with lower thresholds (mFG >= 4 to 6) applicable in Asian and South Asian populations.

source: International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS 2023 (Teede et al., Hum Reprod 2023)
locator: Section 3.1 & 3.2 Cardiovascular and Glycaemic Risk Assessment
text: All individuals with PCOS should have cardiometabolic risk profiling including BMI, waist circumference, and blood pressure monitoring. Glycaemic status (fasting glucose or oral glucose tolerance test / HbA1c) should be evaluated at initial consultation and reassessed every 1 to 3 years based on risk factors, family history, and gestational history. Lipid profiles should be checked to manage atherosclerotic risk.

source: International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS 2023 (Teede et al., Hum Reprod 2023)
text: Lifestyle intervention (incorporating balanced nutrition, tailored physical exercise, and behavioural strategies) is recommended as foundational support for all women with PCOS to optimize metabolic health, energetic vitality, and quality of life. Weight stigma must be actively minimized, focusing on sustainable health habits rather than restrictive dieting.

source: International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS 2023 (Teede et al., Hum Reprod 2023)
locator: Section 2.4 Emotional Wellbeing, Depression, and Anxiety
text: Healthcare professionals should routinely screen all adolescents and women with PCOS for symptoms of depression and anxiety using validated instruments (such as PHQ-9 and GAD-7). When screening identifies elevated psychological distress, appropriate compassionate support and evidence-based mental health referral (including psychological therapy such as cognitive behavioural therapy) should be provided.

source: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JB. The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. J Gen Intern Med 2001;16(9):606-613
locator: PHQ-9 Scoring Table & Item 9 Safety Protocol
text: The Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores depressive symptom frequency over 2 weeks from 0 to 27 (scores 5-9 mild, 10-14 moderate, 15-19 moderately severe, 20-27 severe). Any affirmative response to Item 9 (thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation) mandates immediate clinical safety assessment and emergency crisis helpline linkage.

source: International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS 2023 (Teede et al., Hum Reprod 2023)
text: Women with PCOS have a significantly increased prevalence of obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), independent of body weight. Clinicians should inquire about symptoms including habitual snoring, witnessed breath pauses, unrestful sleep, and daytime hypersomnolence, referring for polysomnography or specialist evaluation when suspected.

text: Preconception assessment should address general health, folic acid supplementation, metabolic status, and cycle frequency. In women seeking pregnancy with anovulatory PCOS, structured evaluation and evidence-based non-pharmacological and pharmacological ovulation induction pathways should be planned in partnership with reproductive healthcare specialists.

source: International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS 2023 (Teede et al., Hum Reprod 2023)
locator: Section 6.1 Long-term Health and Menopausal Transition
text: In the menopausal transition and post-menopause, women with a history of PCOS continue to have elevated risks for cardiovascular events, dyslipidemia, and metabolic conditions. Preventive bone and cardiovascular screening remains important. Any new postmenopausal vaginal bleeding or rapidly developing androgenic symptoms requires prompt clinical evaluation to exclude endometrial hyperplasia or ovarian/adrenal neoplasms.
